A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRGDiff work, and their main text and appendices support reliable comparison. Figure 3 is clipped in v1's page layout, but its complete embedded image is recoverable and matches v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and classification experiments on SEED, SEED-IV and Localize-MI, together with ablations, parameter studies and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds spectral-error measurements, loss-weight sensitivity, computational-cost comparisons, AJILE12 experiments and generalization tests.

M1.justification: Equation 11 changes the stated residual-loss target from z_t minus z_0 to z_0 minus z_t, aligning it with Section 4.2. The architecture and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged. This corrects the documented objective; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: Appendix H.2 adds AJILE12 ECoG channel super-resolution beyond the three retained datasets. Appendix H.3 introduces test-time electrode-subset mismatch, evaluating models trained with 16 or 32 channels on sparser inputs without retraining. These expand the represented data and input conditions.

E2.justification: The six main comparators remain SaSDim, SADI, RDPI, DDPMEEG, ESTformer and STAD. Added comparative experiments reuse ESTformer and STAD. LDM is renamed LDM+LD with unchanged ablation plots and expanded conditioning details, which does not establish a changed comparator.

E3.justification: v2 retains the original random-split evaluation but adds SEED subject holdouts, three session-holdout evaluations, test-time channel subsampling and controlled loss-weight sweeps. It also introduces spectral/topomap error and parameter/FLOPs measurements. The spectral metric is inconsistently described as MAE and NMSE, but the expansion of evaluation protocols is clear.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 newly tests sensitivity to both loss weights. Appendices H.1 and H.3 test robustness to subject/session shifts and missing electrodes at inference. Existing latent-shape, noise-schedule and module ablations are retained; the enlarged topographic figures redisplay existing examples.

E5.justification: The retained experiments still describe mean and standard deviation over subjects. Table 14 newly reports them over folds, with three session holdouts specified in Appendix H.1. Cross-subject fold construction remains unclear because only one subject split is described. No increase in repeated random-seed runs is established.

E6.justification: Main reconstruction, classification and runtime values are retained. v2 adds spectral-error, sensitivity, computational-cost and generalization results in Tables 3 and 10–16; Tables 3 and 11 duplicate the spectral numbers. For example, new AJILE12 results report 2× NMSE of 0.3575 for SRGDiff versus 0.4573 for ESTformer and 0.4932 for STAD. These are added results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The residual-target sign correction in Equation 11 resolves its mathematical inconsistency with the definition and loss in Section 4.2. No new theorem, proof or substantial derivation appears. Equation 9's replacement of gamma with sigma is notation cleanup.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces unspecified gains of up to 40% with roughly 75% relative SNR improvement at 8× against ESTformer and STAD, although Tables 1–2 are unchanged. The introduction narrows transferability to general SR/MDI settings to effectiveness across datasets and SR factors. The central contribution and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of loss-weight extremes, qualifications about subject/session generalization, ECoG applicability, and electrode-layout transfer conditional on a shared coordinate system and latent grid. Appendix G also adds computational tradeoff interpretations, although its claim that SRGDiff requires more FLOPs than ESTformer contradicts Table 12.

D1.justification: The reported code link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. New disclosures explain the LDM+LD baseline's static guidance, electrode-coordinate projection onto a latent grid, and matched hardware/batch conditions for timing. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the existing implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Peterson et al. (2022) for AJILE12 and relates the ECoG evaluation to Vetter et al. (2024). Section 2's substantive positioning against earlier diffusion, EEG super-resolution and residual-guidance methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 revises abstract and contribution wording, expands abbreviations and the STFT explanation, standardizes citation formatting, separates the evaluation protocol into a subsection, and groups feature-level evaluation together. It adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections, while retaining most existing prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds several result tables and a baseline schematic, relocates Figure 3 so it is fully visible, and enlarges and splits v1's Figure 4 between Figures 4 and 15. It also merges the SEED/SEED-IV latent-shape tables and updates ablation legends. These substantially revise presentation, including redisplayed and newly added material.

improvement.justification: The added subject/session holdouts and electrode-removal tests make applicability more assessable than v1's random-split evaluation. Correcting Equation 11, clarifying the baseline and restoring Figure 3's visibility also improve the paper. However, inconsistent MAE/NMSE definitions and the FLOPs discussion contradicting Table 12 weaken the new evidence, limiting the net improvement.
